bluetooth_classic.notes: The official serial guide defines the framing and DataRows. The current vendor Classic transport feeds each received byte to the same parser family, while its BLE transport is a different protocol and is intentionally absent here.

profiles.notes: Secure socket after the host's normal bond. Resolve the RFCOMM channel by SDP. The independent Python client's channel 1 is recorded only in protocol_details.

framing.notes: AA AA, then PLENGTH, PAYLOAD[PLENGTH], CHECKSUM. PLENGTH counts only the payload and is valid from 0 through 169; a complete packet is PLENGTH+4 bytes. CHECKSUM is (~sum(PAYLOAD)) & 0xff. Keep one buffer across socket reads, enforce the 169-byte limit before allocation, and never parse DataRows before checksum verification. After an oversized length or bad checksum discard only the first buffered byte and resume scanning for AA AA, because a candidate packet may itself contain the sync pair. Single-byte length fields have no endianness; the value 0x00 is valid for an empty payload.

serial.notes: Asynchronous stream, not a request/reply command channel. Read a complete valid packet before considering any firmware-specific configuration. No write is required for the basic eSense/raw/EEG surface and no command is declared here.

methods.notes: Enter pairing mode before inquiry. SPP narrows the exact-name match; SPP alone would identify nothing. Open the socket by SDP UUID, not by assuming the independent client's channel 1 on every unit.

host_compatibility.basis: The current vendor SDK can open a secure RFCOMM socket by the standard SPP UUID after bonding. That code does not establish Mobile 2 radio support and is used only as transport evidence.
robintibor/python-mindwave-mobile, MIT, opens an RFCOMM socket to the exact original name and parses ThinkGear packets. Its fixed channel 1 is not treated as an SDP invariant.

The documented control surface is RFCOMM/SPP, which CoreBluetooth does not expose. The 2011 guide mentions iOS pairing but does not establish an MFi/iAP2 protocol that an independent client could use.
host_compatibility.notes: This verdict is limited to an independent CoreBluetooth client on iOS/iPadOS. It does not deny the historical vendor iOS apps, whose accessory mechanism is unresolved. macOS is separate: IOBluetooth provides Classic RFCOMM.

identification.notes: This is a Classic-only target: the inquiry/remote name is exactly "MindWave Mobile". Do not put that name in a BLE identification key and do not claim a Mobile 2 merely because a BLE scan prints the same text.

device.name: NeuroSky MindWave Mobile (original)
device.notes:
Scope is the ORIGINAL MindWave Mobile, FCC ID XG9MW3, whose control surface is Bluetooth Classic RFCOMM/SPP carrying ThinkGear serial packets. MindWave Mobile 2 uses a different BLE characteristic/command surface and is NOT covered. The older USB-dongle MindWave generation (XG9MW1/XG9MW2) is also excluded.
A phone or PC opens SPP by UUID 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb after standard OS Bluetooth pairing. An independent Linux client used RFCOMM channel 1; that is legacy evidence, not a universal SDP guarantee, so resolve the channel by SDP first. The stream is asynchronous and read-only here. Do not copy Mobile 2's 20-byte BLE command wrapper or its raw-output/notch commands onto this hardware. Official ThinkGear configuration bytes are firmware-specific and can make a module unresponsive until power-cycled; none is declared as a safe command in this spec.

openness.notes: The serial format is vendor-published. The original Mobile's name, bonding and SPP path are corroborated by the official guide and independent clients; transport selection and cross-generation behavior remain reconstructed.

upstream_docs.covers: Packet sync, the 169-byte payload limit, checksum, DataRows, raw samples and ASIC EEG powers.

exclusivity.notes: The official guide states a three-host pairing memory.
exclusivity.recovery: Disconnect the old host first. If a new host cannot pair, clear all pairing memory with the documented hold, then pair again. The headset remembers up to three hosts, so adding one is not inherently a single-bond replacement.

pairing.notes: Confidence is medium because the vendor guide gives the complete flow, but no procedure here is marked verified: this project did not execute it.

pin.notes: From the official XG9MW3 guide; used only if the host asks.

unpair.clears: All remembered hosts at once; no per-host erase is documented.
unpair.notes: This is the same operation recorded under factory_reset, not a separate per-host unpair.

procedures.name: Clear the pairing memory with the power switch

steps.action: Hold the switch past ON for ten seconds, then release it.
steps.expect: Every old host bond is forgotten; other device behavior is unchanged.

safety_advisory.detail: eSense Attention and Meditation are vendor-defined wellness metrics. Raw EEG and band powers have no clinical interpretation in this spec. Do not use this unverified client to make health, safety or treatment decisions.
safety_advisory.summary: Experimental wellness telemetry, not a medical or diagnostic measurement.

credentials.notes: Legacy PIN 0000 is a product-wide pairing convention, not an application encryption key. There is no Wi-Fi, vendor account token or cloud credential.
stored_on_device: Up to three Bluetooth Classic bonds

factory_reset.description: The user guide has no broader data-reset procedure. Its reference section says holding past ON for six seconds clears pairing memory; a quick-start passage says ten seconds. The procedure below uses the longer instruction and records the conflict rather than hiding it. Power-cycling restores the ThinkGear module's default output configuration after any unsupported command.
factory_reset.effect: Clears all remembered Bluetooth hosts (up to three). It does not install firmware or erase health history, because no such history surface is claimed.

procedures.basis: NeuroSky XG9MW3 user guide: pairing-memory instructions in the quick-start and reference sections, which give ten and six seconds respectively.
procedures.indicator: No distinct completion indication is documented.
procedures.name: Clear all remembered Bluetooth pairings

steps.action: Hold the power switch past ON for ten seconds, then release it.
steps.expect: All previously remembered hosts are cleared; the headset must be paired again.

steps.action: Enter pairing mode again with a three-second hold and pair the new host.
steps.expect: The blue LED flashes, then becomes solid on connection.

methods.description: Slide the switch to ON, hold it past ON for three seconds to enter pairing mode (release before six seconds), select MindWave Mobile in the host's Bluetooth settings, enter 0000 if prompted, then open SPP by UUID.

steps.action: Insert one AAA battery and slide the power switch to ON.
steps.expect: The status LED lights; pairing mode normally starts automatically.

steps.action: Hold the switch past ON for three seconds, then release it before six seconds.
steps.expect: The blue LED flashes during the roughly two-minute pairing window.

steps.action: Select exactly MindWave Mobile in the host Bluetooth settings and enter legacy PIN 0000 if asked.
steps.expect: The blue LED becomes solid after pairing/connection.

steps.action: Resolve SPP 00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb through SDP and open a secure RFCOMM socket.
steps.expect: ThinkGear packets arrive as a byte stream; keep it passive before attempting any configuration.

causes: The application opened the wrong RFCOMM channel. Resolve SPP with SDP; channel 1 is only one independent client's legacy observation.
The host is connected but the client has not enabled raw output. This spec sends no cross-generation enable command; establish the original unit's firmware behavior first.

causes: The switch was held past ON for six seconds or longer, which clears all remembered hosts. Re-pair from scratch.
troubleshooting.symptom: The pairing memory is unexpectedly empty.

setup.notes: The official 2011 guide documents OS pairing, legacy PIN 0000 when asked, and a serial/COM connection. Medium confidence in the documented flow, but this project has not replayed it; setup.methods[].verified therefore remains false.

rejoin.notes: A previously bonded host reconnects without provisioning. For a new host, enter pairing mode again; clear all remembered hosts only when adoption fails.

steps.action: Turn the headset on and open its SPP service from the bonded host.
steps.expect: Solid blue LED and a ThinkGear byte stream.

testing.notes: No headset was paired or driven from this document. Protocol facts come from the official guide/manual and public implementations; no private EEG recording is held. This spec deliberately claims no Mobile 2 BLE support.

variants.notes: The only covered model. Do not infer Mobile 2 BLE support from this entry and do not apply the adjacent XG9MW1/XG9MW2 USB-dongle generation's manuals.

artifacts.description: Authoritative packet/DataRow formats and command warnings.
Model-specific pairing and serial/COM instructions; adjacent XG9MW1/XG9MW2 are excluded.
Original-name RFCOMM client and ThinkGear parser.

evidence.negative_findings: No OTA/firmware-update surface was established. No evidence makes Mobile 2 BLE characteristics valid on the original, proves every Mobile 2 exposes Classic, or establishes a cross-generation raw-enable/notch command table.
evidence.official_documentation: NeuroSky's ThinkGear Serial Stream Guide supplies packet framing, PLENGTH <=169, one's-complement checksum, DataRow extension/length rules, signed big-endian raw samples and eight big-endian 24-bit band powers. The 2011 XG9MW3 user guide supplies pairing, legacy PIN, three-host memory, pairing-mode LED/timing and pairing-memory clearing. No health data was collected.
evidence.open_questions: The original unit's SDP record/channel, exact command support, maximum simultaneous serial connections, and the historical iOS accessory mechanism need owner captures.
evidence.public_implementations: robintibor/python-mindwave-mobile at b2bedb56f1e3b249a69ee669378f2e505c495091 corroborates the original name and RFCOMM path. Current vendor transport code corroborates SPP-by-UUID and the complement checksum; its BLE-only formats are excluded rather than generalized.

command_boundary.excluded: Mobile 2 BLE characteristics, its 20-byte command envelope, raw-enable 0x15 and 50/60 Hz selectors 0x1b/0x1c. Official ASIC page-0 bytes are firmware specific and no original-unit capture supports declaring one here.

codes.name: battery
codes.notes: Present in the official example; scale is device-specific and not claimed here.

codes.name: poor_signal
codes.notes: 0 is good; larger means noisier. 200 specifically means no skin contact.

codes.name: attention
codes.notes: 1-100 relative scale; 0 means unavailable/unreliable, not minimum attention.

codes.name: blink_strength
codes.notes: Reported by the current parser; official serial guide says it is not directly available from current ThinkGear hardware, so do not require it.

codes.name: raw_eeg
codes.notes: Signed two's-complement ADC counts. No microvolt scale is established; do not assign one.

codes.name: asic_eeg_power
codes.notes: Dimensionless relative band-power values; not clinical measurements.

datarow.layout: Zero or more 0x55 extended-code bytes, CODE, optional VLENGTH, VALUE.
datarow.length_rule: CODE < 0x80: one-byte VALUE and no VLENGTH. CODE >= 0x80: a one-byte VLENGTH followed by that many VALUE bytes.
datarow.unknown_rule: Skip an unknown (extended-level, CODE) row using the same length rule; unknown does not invalidate neighboring rows. A truncated row invalidates the packet rather than exposing a partial value.

legacy_channel_one.notes: An independent Linux client opens RFCOMM channel 1. Prefer SDP and use this only as a fallback after inspecting the unit's own record.

packet.fragmentation: Arbitrary RFCOMM read boundaries, including one byte at a time and several packets coalesced.
packet.malformed_input: Reject bad length/checksum without emitting any row; then scan forward one byte at a time for the next AA AA.

thinkgear_stream.renderer: A consumer needs a ThinkGear stream parser; fixed-offset GATT-style entities cannot represent variable DataRows and are deliberately not fabricated.

test_vectors.name: Official guide example (illustrative values, not a recording)
Synthetic common rows and unknown extension
test_vectors.packet_note: Packet framing/checksum is computed by the independent test. The 0x55 extended-code level and unknown 0x90 row must not stop later 0x83 decoding.

remaining_unknowns: The original headset's SDP record and whether channel 1 is consistent across production units.
Which configuration bytes each original firmware accepts, and how to enable raw output safely on a unit that has it disabled.
Whether more than one host may hold the RFCOMM link simultaneously.
How the historical iOS apps reached this Classic model (MFi/iAP2 or another path); CoreBluetooth alone cannot open SPP.
Physical units and scaling of the raw ADC counts and battery byte; neither is assigned an invented engineering unit.
